steps.title: Identify the noun’s case role
steps.body: In the supplied Муж говорит, the husband is the subject and the talking verb states its action. The subject noun is nominative. Recognizing the English sentence meaning is useful, but the role check asks whether the noun is a subject or direct object. Do not guess nominative merely because a case is unfamiliar.

steps.title: Separate the subject from its description
steps.body: In Поезд старый, the train is the subject noun and old is its predicate description. This present property clause has no overt Russian copula. The noun’s case role is nominative subject, not accusative direct object. A dictionary-looking noun or familiar translation alone does not identify its role in every construction.

steps.title: Apply the distinction to a different supplied noun
steps.body: Студент новый supplies a second independent property clause: the student is the subject noun, and new describes that subject. Its case role is nominative subject. Keep Муж говорит — The husband is talking and Поезд старый — The train is old as correct sentence meanings; the optional reference choices do not demonstrate this case role. These supplied examples are deliberately taught, not unseen evidence or unrestricted productive case use. Other constructions have nominative predicate nouns; not every nominative noun is a subject.

steps.title: Match we in the supplied speaking forms
steps.body: The infinitive говори́ть names this entry. Match each supplied present form to its person: I: говорю́; you (one familiar person): говори́шь; he: говори́т; we: говори́м. When the check requests we, choose говори́м. Compare the written endings in these supplied forms; do not substitute the endings from the earlier reading example. First practise a different person from this same entry, then answer the requested person without using option position. These supplied choices do not demonstrate producing an unseen form.

steps.title: Match he in the supplied seeing forms
steps.body: The infinitive ви́деть names this entry. Match each supplied present form to its person: I: ви́жу; you (one familiar person): ви́дишь; he: ви́дит; we: ви́дим. When the check requests he, choose ви́дит. The infinitive alone does not tell you which supplied form to choose. Notice that the I form differs from the other forms here; learn the whole supplied forms. First practise a different person from this same entry, then answer the requested person without using option position. These supplied choices do not demonstrate producing an unseen form.

steps.title: Match you (plural) in the supplied writing forms
steps.body: The infinitive писа́ть names this entry. Match each supplied present form to its person: I: пишу́; you (one familiar person): пи́шешь; he: пи́шет; you (plural): пи́шете. When the check requests you (plural), choose пи́шете. The supplied present forms have a different written stem from the infinitive. Keep the written stress exactly as shown; do not append an ending to the whole infinitive. First practise a different person from this same entry, then answer the requested person without using option position. These supplied choices do not demonstrate producing an unseen form.
